options.text: Count the ice-cream sticks that make up each whole shape; repeating that same count gives $5$, $9$, $13$, $\ldots$.
Count the sticks in Shape $1$ only, then reuse that same count for every later shape.
The same structural feature — the sticks of each whole frame — must be counted in every shape of the sequence.
Pick the printed numeral $13$ alone because it is the largest number shown.

stem:
Parth builds a row of pentagon frames with ice-cream sticks. Shape $1$ uses $5$ sticks, Shape $2$ uses $9$ sticks, and Shape $3$ uses $13$ sticks.

Which two claims correctly name the countable feature that produces the related number sequence $5$, $9$, $13$, $\ldots$?

teacher.key_rationale: The related sequence is made by counting the same structural feature in every shape: the sticks of each whole pentagon frame (5, then 9, then 13). Reusing only Shape 1's count drops the later shapes. The largest printed numeral is not the countable feature.
